name: ZenQori Webhook Chat for n8n
author: ZenQori

sections.description:
ZenQori Webhook Chat for n8n adds a lightweight chat widget to WordPress. You provide the production webhook URL from an active n8n Chat Trigger workflow and the plugin sends visitor messages directly to that endpoint.

The plugin includes its own local JavaScript and CSS. It does not load executable code from a third-party CDN.

Features:

  • Connect to an n8n Chat Trigger production webhook.
  • Custom chat title and welcome message.
  • Custom input placeholder and primary color.
  • Bottom-left or bottom-right placement.
  • Choice of chat icons (chat bubble, robot, sparkle, headset and more), your own image, five icon sizes and an optional icon in the chat header.
  • Persistent browser session ID so n8n memory nodes can associate messages with a session.
  • No ZenQori account is required to use the WordPress plugin.

External service

This plugin connects to an external webhook URL configured by the WordPress administrator. It is designed for n8n Chat Trigger endpoints, which may be hosted by n8n Cloud, by the site owner, or by another hosting provider.

When the chatbot is enabled and a visitor sends a message, the visitor’s browser sends the following data to the configured webhook endpoint:

  • The visitor’s chat message (chatInput).
  • A randomly generated browser session identifier (sessionId).
  • The action name (sendMessage).

ZenQori does not receive or process chat messages. Messages are sent directly from the visitor’s browser to the webhook URL selected and configured by the website administrator.

Because the webhook destination is selected by the administrator, the site owner is responsible for reviewing the privacy policy, terms, data location, retention, and legal basis applicable to that endpoint and any AI/model services used by the connected workflow.

n8n website: https://n8n.io/
n8n privacy policy: https://n8n.io/legal/privacy/
n8n terms: https://n8n.io/legal/
ZenQori information: https://zenqori.com/

This plugin is an independent integration and is not affiliated with or endorsed by n8n.

Privacy

The plugin stores a randomly generated chat session identifier in the visitor’s browser local storage. It does not create a WordPress database record for visitor chat messages.

When a visitor submits a message, the message and session identifier are sent to the webhook URL configured by the site administrator. The external workflow may process, store, forward, or enrich this data depending on its configuration. Site administrators should disclose this processing in their own privacy policy where required.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install the ZIP through WordPress Admin > Plugins > Add Plugin > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate “ZenQori Webhook Chat for n8n”.
  3. Open Settings > ZenQori n8n Chat.
  4. Paste the production webhook URL from your active n8n Chat Trigger.
  5. In the n8n Chat Trigger, allow your WordPress site’s origin (CORS/Allowed Origins).
  6. Customize the title, welcome message, color, position and chat icon.
  7. Enable the chatbot and save the settings.
sections.faq:
Do I need a ZenQori account?

No. The plugin works with a compatible n8n Chat Trigger webhook URL configured by the site administrator.

Does the plugin send my visitors’ messages to ZenQori?

No. ZenQori does not receive or process chat messages. Messages are sent directly from the visitor’s browser to the webhook URL selected and configured by the website administrator.

Why does the chatbot show an error after I send a message?

Confirm that the n8n workflow is active, that you are using the production Chat Trigger webhook URL, and that your WordPress domain is permitted in the Chat Trigger Allowed Origins setting.

What request does the widget send?

It sends a JSON POST request containing action: sendMessage, sessionId, and chatInput, matching the standard n8n Chat Trigger message fields.

Does this plugin load JavaScript from a CDN?

No. The widget JavaScript and CSS are included locally in the plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • New: choose the chat launcher icon from several presets, the ZenQori logo or your own image, pick its size and show it in the chat header. The existing emoji icon stays the default.
  • The plugin is now named ZenQori Webhook Chat for n8n. The plugin address and settings are unchanged.

1.1.4

  • Plain URLs in assistant replies are now clickable.
  • Markdown links split across two lines are now rendered as one link.
  • Fixed readme Contributors field.
  • Fixed rendering of links and images placed inside bold text in assistant replies.
  • Removed bundled translation files; translations are now delivered through translate.wordpress.org.

1.1.2

  • Updated plugin author branding to ZenQori.
  • Clarified webhook and privacy wording: ZenQori does not operate or receive customer chat traffic.

1.1.1

  • Render assistant Markdown as formatted content.
  • Add safe clickable links and product images.
  • Add styles for lists, headings, links, code and responsive images.
  • Keep user/status/error messages as plain text.

1.1.0

  • Added WordPress Privacy Policy helper content for chatbot data processing.
  • Localized the default chat title, welcome message, and input placeholder.
  • Improved internationalization support and updated bundled translations.
  • Updated plugin version metadata to 1.1.0.

1.0.0

  • Initial ZenQori release.
  • Local, dependency-free chat widget.
  • n8n Chat Trigger webhook integration.
  • Configurable title, welcome text, input placeholder, color, and position.
  • Privacy and external-service disclosure.
